title: Practical SBB Encryption with Boundary Hiding and DoS Resistance
summary: Because never returning failure is impractical and DoS-prone, it remains open to construct a practical sbb encryption scheme achieving both BH-sbbCFA and DOS-sbbCFA security.

formal_statement.body: In the stateless-beyond-buffering (sbb) setting for symmetric encryption under ciphertext fragmentation, construct a practical encryption scheme that simultaneously achieves active ciphertext boundary hiding, denoted $\mathrm{BH\text{-}sbbCFA}$, and denial-of-service resistance, denoted $\mathrm{DOS\text{-}sbbCFA}$. This task addresses the impracticality and denial-of-service exposure of prohibiting the decryption algorithm from ever returning $\bot$.

scope.domain: Symmetric encryption under ciphertext fragmentation in the stateless-beyond-buffering model.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a practical encryption scheme that simultaneously satisfies active boundary-hiding security (BH-sbbCFA) and denial-of-service resistance (DOS-sbbCFA).

citations.label: Security of Symmetric Encryption in the Presence of Ciphertext Fragmentation

progress.summary: The source notes that forbidding decryption from returning failure is impractical and vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks, then explicitly poses a practical scheme satisfying both security notions as an open question.
citation_labels: Alexandra Boldyreva et al., Security of Symmetric Encryption in the Presence of Ciphertext Fragmentation
